 A Loving Farewell: RJ Mitte Remembered at Convention Following His Passing
 A Space for Remembrance Costars Gather in His Honor A Life of Purpose Beyond the Screen Tributes From His Breaking Bad Family A Heartfelt Plea for Mental Health His Legacy Lives On
 By Mark Lim Published a day ago • 3 min read DALLAS — The halls of NTX Universe 2026 became more than a venue for collectibles and celebrity encounters this past weekend; they became a sacred space of remembrance. What was meant to be a joyful appearance by beloved actor RJ Mitte turned into a tender tribute after the 34‑year‑old Breaking Bad star passed away on October 12. From Friday, October 16 through Sunday, October 18, fans, friends, and former castmates gathered to honour his life, his warmth, and the profound impact he made both on and off screen.
 A Space for Remembrance
 Mitte had been scheduled to meet fans and sign autographs at the event. Instead, organisers made the thoughtful decision to leave his table standing, transformed into a quiet memorial where attendees could pause, reflect, and write messages of love and sympathy in condolence books to be delivered to his family. “We are heartbroken to share that RJ Mitte has passed away,” the convention shared in a touching announcement. “His table at NTX Universe will remain in place as a memorial. Fans are welcome to stop by and leave a note.” The gesture struck a chord, turning loss into connection as hundreds poured out their gratitude and affection.
 Costars Gather in His Honor
 The weekend concluded with a poignant moment as three of Mitte’s Breaking Bad castmates, Giancarlo Esposito , Raymond Cruz , and Daniel Moncada, joined his longtime friend and agent, Ben Brucato , to stand together before the memorial. Brucato captured the moment in a heartfelt post: “This weekend in Dallas was bittersweet. RJ was supposed to be there with us, and it was hard knowing he wasn’t. His absence was felt throughout the weekend, and things just weren’t the same without him.” He thanked the convention organisers for their kindness and added, “It was a thoughtful gesture that meant a lot, and I’m grateful for all the love and support shown to RJ and his family this weekend.”
 A Life of Purpose Beyond the Screen
 To the world, Mitte will forever be known as Walter White Jr. the resilient young man at the heart of one of television’s greatest dramas. But his greatest role extended far beyond the camera. Born with cerebral palsy, he refused to let his condition define or limit him. He became a powerful advocate for disability rights, accessibility, and inclusion, using his platform to speak up for those often overlooked. “He never ever allowed that challenge to be an excuse for anything,” Bryan Cranston would later write. Mitte turned personal adversity into public service, becoming a voice, a role model, and a source of pride for millions.
 Tributes From His Breaking Bad Family
 As news of his passing spread, those who knew him best shared their grief and gratitude:
 Bryan Cranston , who played his father on screen, remembered meeting Mitte at just 14 years old. “He met the demanding shooting schedule head-on with great determination,” Cranston wrote. “My sweet son on Breaking Bad has died.”
 Anna Gunn , his on‑screen mother, called him her “beloved TV son” and spoke of watching him grow: “How lucky we were that RJ came into the Breaking Bad family and lit up our lives… I was so proud of him; we all were.” She celebrated his tireless advocacy and philanthropic work, noting how he continued to serve his community long after the cameras stopped rolling.
 It was later confirmed that Mitte died by suicide, a reality that has deepened the sorrow but also sharpened the focus on what we can learn from his loss.
 A Heartfelt Plea for Mental Health
 Brucato closed his message with words that resonate far beyond fandom: “I also want to take a moment to remind everyone that mental health matters. You never really know what someone is going through behind closed doors, so please check on your people, even the ones who seem like they’re doing okay.” He offered hope and help to anyone struggling: “Call or text 988 to reach the Suicide & Crisis Lifeline. There is help, there is hope, and your life matters.”
 His Legacy Lives On
 RJ Mitte may have left the stage too soon, but his light has not gone out. It shines in the barriers he broke, the voices he lifted, and the kindness he showed everyone he met. At NTX Universe, and across the world, people are not just mourning his passing they are carrying forward his message: to be kinder, to look deeper, and to reach out before it’s too late. Rest peacefully, RJ. You will not be forgotten.
